props.name: name
props.description: The person's name. It is the accessible name of the image and the source of the initials — one field, so the two cannot disagree.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter. An avatar is square by ratio, so `size` is one axis.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source. Without it, the initials render.

ai.summary: A circular portrait of a person, with initials derived from their name as the fallback.
whenToUse: A list or header identifies a person by their picture
An account menu, comment, or assignment shows who it belongs to
Several people are stacked in a group — see the Avatar Group entry
whenNotToUse: It is a company or project logo — that is an image, not a person
It is clickable — wrap it in a Button or Link; an avatar takes no interaction
The name is unknown and the picture is decorative — use a plain image with `alt=""`
ai.accessibility: The host carries `role="img"` and the person's name as its accessible name, so the picture is announced as the person rather than as a filename or as nothing. The `` inside is `alt=""` and the initials are `aria-hidden`, because one announcement of a person is better than two competing ones. An avatar with neither a name nor initials is `aria-hidden` instead of an empty `role="img"` — an unnamed image is an axe violation, and defaulting the label to a word like "avatar" would announce the designer's word instead of the person's name. `data-state` distinguishes `absent` from `error`, which render identical pixels and are two different bugs.
knownLimitations: Initials take the first and last word only — name order, particles, and single-name cultures are locale questions, and §6 says locale is consumer-supplied
There is no `initials` prop: they are derived from `name`, so the two cannot disagree
`size` sets the diameter; the frame is square by ratio, so there is no separate width and height
